description: Editable fictional policies for developing and simulating an airline customer service agent. All amounts, allowances, and deadlines are invented sample values, not any real airline's policies or a statement of passenger rights.

scope.partner_operated_flights: Not covered. Confirm the operating carrier's policies.

route_classification.domestic: Every segment in the ticketed direction stays within one country.
route_classification.international: At least one segment in the ticketed direction crosses a country border. Apply the international table to that whole direction, including its domestic connections.

scope.fee_amounts: Final fictional amounts in USD, including any applicable sample taxes. Each fee states its own charging unit.
scope.time_reference: Deadlines are relative to the scheduled departure of the relevant flight segment, using the departure airport's local time.
scope.exceptions: Confirmed itinerary-specific or airport-specific requirements take precedence. If a required exception is not documented, obtain confirmation rather than inventing a rule.
scope.policy_selection: Apply fare-dependent baggage, cancellation, and change rules using the purchased fare_tier, not seat_class alone. Premium economy standard follows standard rules; premium economy flexible follows flexible rules. The business cabin offers only the business tier.
scope.fee_and_fare_conversion: Policy fees are stated in USD dollars. Database price_cents values are USD cents: 8900 cents is USD 89.00. Convert to a common unit before combining a ticket price with optional fees. Included baggage allowances are already part of the purchased fare.

inventory_reference.live_data: Use current database records for flight schedules, flight status, available seats, and fare quotes. The seed file is a starting dataset, not live inventory; do not hard-code its prices or availability into policy answers.
inventory_reference.shared_inventory: All fare tiers in one flight cabin use the same available_seats count. A sold-out cabin has no bookable tier; a more expensive tier does not create additional seats.
inventory_reference.sample_week_scope: The sample week describes the available seed flights; it is not an expiry date or travel-date restriction for these policies.
inventory_reference.untracked_services: Flight seat inventory does not track pet-carrier availability, approved medical devices, mobility-aid acceptance, or confirmed special assistance. Those arrangements require separate confirmation.

policy.title: Rescheduling and flight changes
policy.summary: Voluntary changes depend on fare type and may require a change fee and fare difference. Airline disruption rebooking follows a separate rule.
questions_to_ask: Which cabin and fare tier did you purchase, and is the journey domestic or international?
What are the original departure time and requested replacement flights?
Is the change voluntary or caused by an airline disruption?
Was the ticket purchased directly, and has any segment been used?

rules.title: Voluntary changes before departure
rules.answer: For a wholly unused directly booked ticket, basic does not allow voluntary flight changes; cancellation and a new purchase are separate options under the cancellation policy. Standard permits changes before the original first scheduled departure for USD 30 domestically or USD 60 internationally, plus any positive fare difference. Flexible and business charge no change fee, but any positive fare difference still applies. Availability and the replacement fare must be confirmed before quoting the total. These change rules follow the purchased fare tier, including standard and flexible fares in premium economy.

details.change_fee_separate_from_negative_fare_d: The applicable change fee is still due. A lower replacement fare does not waive it.
details.partially_used_or_third_party_tickets: Require an individual fare assessment or the issuing seller.
details.replacement_fare_selection: Select the replacement flight_id, seat_class, and fare_tier together.
details.fare_comparison: Compare original paid ticket value and current replacement fare for the same passenger and segment scope in the same currency. Never substitute the current price of the original flight for the original paid amount.
details.missing_paid_value: Original ticket payment records are not in the flight inventory tables. Confirm that amount before quoting a fare difference.

rules.title: Disruption rebooking and late changes
rules.answer: Rebooking after a qualifying airline disruption follows the disruption policy, which waives change fees and fare differences for available replacement travel. Requests at or after the original scheduled departure require assessment under the no-show rules. Do not apply the voluntary change-fee table automatically to either situation.
